headline: Move to Node.js 24.22.1 for the CVE-2026-111497 Brotli decoder fix
summary: Node.js 24.22.1 fixes CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js that malformed compressed data can trigger, and nine other vulnerabilities in DNS, TLS, HTTP, crypto and the Permission Model. The container image now refuses to build with an older Node, and the server refuses to start on one.

items.title: Run on Node.js 24.22.1
items.body: The container image installs `nodejs-24` 24.22.1 or newer on the wolfi-base image of 2026-10-26. Node.js 24.22.1 fixes CVE-2026-111497, in which invalid Brotli data writes past an 8-byte buffer and can crash the process, disclose memory or run code. Node.js 24.22.1 also fixes CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069 and CVE-2026-106072 in `tls.checkServerIdentity()`, CVE-2026-105482 in `dns.resolve*()`, CVE-2026-105481 in HTTP keep-alive sockets, CVE-2026-106074 in `crypto.randomUUID()` for snapshot builds, and CVE-2026-106073 in the Permission Model, and it updates the bundled OpenSSL, c-ares, Undici and CA certificates.

items.title: Node.js floor moves to 24.22.1
items.body:
Running from source on Node older than 24.22.1 now exits at startup with a message naming the version found. Earlier releases checked only the major and minor version, so 24.22.0 passed; the check now compares the patch version too.

If you run the container image, pull the new image. The `nodejs-24` package in the image is installed with a `>=24.22.1` constraint, so a build that cannot get a fixed Node fails. If you installed with `deploy/install.sh`, re-run it or upgrade Node through your package manager. NodeSource `setup_24.x` ships a current 24.x.
